beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Riley lays out all three cards together for the first time.

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: The past: the songs, quietly growing.

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: The present: the leap you already took.

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: The future: the partnership you're weighing.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Okay, quiz me back then. If the Empress is about something quietly growing, why didn't it show up back when I first started writing those songs?"

options.text: It was already there — the past doesn't wait to be drawn.
It didn't exist yet at that point.
The Empress only applies going forward.

elaboration: A card in the past position isn't dated to the moment you draw it — the songs were already quietly alive long before you ever sat down for a reading.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "And the Fool — does 'present' mean I'm still mid-leap, or that I've landed on this tour by now?"

options.text: Still mid-leap — the Fool doesn't mark a landing.
It means you've definitely landed safely.
It means the leap already failed.

elaboration: The Fool never shows the landing, only the jump — 'present' just means you're still in the air, not that it's over one way or the other.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "And if I turn down the writing partnership — does that undo the leap I already took joining this tour?"

options.text: No — the leap already happened either way.
Yes, saying no erases the whole reading.
The Lovers card doesn't allow saying no.

elaboration: The Lovers only asks you to weigh this one choice carefully — whichever way you go, it doesn't reach back and unmake the leap you already took.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "One more — is the whole point of the Empress that I should've shared the songs with people sooner?"

options.text: No — the point is you cared for them before anyone judged them.
Yes, secrecy is always the wrong move.
The Empress has no opinion on secrecy either way.

elaboration: Nourish and protect first, before it's ready for anyone else's opinion — that's the actual message, not a verdict on when you should have gone public.

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: One thread ties all three: the songs you grew quietly, the leap that put them on a stage, and a choice that doesn't have to be forced to be right.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Thanks. I think that's the real lesson — the songs I quietly built, the leap that got me here, and whatever I choose next all belong together, and none of it needed to be perfect to count. That actually means a lot."
